description: AstraQuest is a team of passionate young innovators driven by curiosity, creativity, and a shared ambition to explore beyond Earth. We aim to turn complex space challenges into interactive learning experiences, inspiring the next generation of explorers through science, technology, and teamwork. Our mission is to make space exploration more accessible, engaging, and educational, one challenge at a time.
summary: Built with real NASA Mars Trek and Perseverance Rover data, AstraQuest turns NASA science into playable leadership decisions for students. Made as a website so anyone can play in 1 click - no download needed
details: What does it do / How does it work?AstraQuest: Jezero - Sol 30 Edition is a 3D Mars colony survival simulation. The player is the Mission Commander at Jezero Crater and must keep 6 astronauts alive for 30 Martian sols.The player manages 4 live resources: Power, Oxygen, Food, and Shield. They assign daily tasks to 6 crew members with different skills. Every Sol, the game throws one of 6 unexpected crises based on real Mars conditions: Dust Storm, Power Failure, Oxygen Leak, Communication Blackout, Food Shortage, and Radiation Spike.Every choice changes the 4 resources. If any resource hits 0%, you lose a crew member. There is no single winning strategy.What benefits does it have? What is the intended impact?We turn hard NASA data into playable decisions. Instead of reading about Mars, students live it.For high school students in Egypt and worldwide, it makes physics, math, and space science simple: they learn resource management, 38% Mars gravity, solar power, and life support systems by playing, not memorizing. Our goal is to make NASA science accessible to Arabic-speaking students and to inspire more girls in STEM to lead space missions.What tools, languages, software did you use?Engine: Construct 3 for 3D game logic and HTML5 exportWebsite: Canva / Google Sites for the final submission websiteData: Real NASA data - Mars Trek, Jezero Crater topography, Perseverance Rover weather data, NASA Power Systems and Life Support dataDesign: Figma for UI, Tinkercad for Habitat and Rover conceptsNo hardware needed, runs on any phone or laptop via Website linkHow is your project creative?Most Mars games are shooting or driving. Ours is leadership. You don't win by killing, you win by keeping people alive.We used 6 real NASA mission systems - Power, Habitat, Life Support, Mobility, Communication, Safety - as the 6 game levels. And we added a moral system: sometimes you must choose to save Oxygen OR save Power. That choice has consequences.What factors did your team consider?Real Science: Used real Jezero Crater location, real 30-sol cycle, real 38% gravity effect on energy.Accessibility: Made it a Website, not an App, so any judge can play in 1 click without downloading.Education: Made it playable for high school students with no science background.Teamwork: 6 astronauts = 6 different roles, so players learn crew management.
